title: SF3000 Procedure
description: An ordered set of steps too long or too disruptive for one fix, such as a release upgrade. Each step is checked, run and verified on its own, and the machine may reboot between steps. The engine runs the steps from a root-owned copy under a system service, so they carry on after each reboot.

check.description: A read-only question about the machine and the answer that counts as yes. Same rules as a playbook's detect and expect.

command.description: READ-ONLY command. Must not mutate the system.

description.description: One plain-language line: what this step does.

requires.description: Optional precondition, checked just before the step runs. If it does not hold, the procedure stops without running the step.

detect.description: READ-ONLY. With expect, answers: has this step's goal been reached? A step whose goal is already reached is skipped, and the same check verifies the step after it runs (after the reboot, when reboot_after is true).

run.description: The step's vetted command(s), keyed by distro or 'default'. Run verbatim, with no terminal: it must not ask questions.

timeout_minutes.description: How long the command may run. When it is exceeded, the engine stops the command and the procedure. Set it generously: a step stopped halfway may leave the machine needing its snapshot.

reboot_after.description: Reboot once the command exits 0, and verify the step after the machine comes back.

description.description: One-line, plain-language statement of what the procedure does.

symptoms.description: Free-text user complaints, used only for matching. Never executed.

requires_privilege.description: Always true: the engine installs a system service to carry the procedure across reboots.

strategy.description: snapshot_only = the only way back is a snapshot or backup taken before the start; the engine refuses to start until the person names one. none = nothing to undo.

source.description: Provenance: who vetted this and where it was tested.
